attributes.title: Junior Client Success Manager
attributes.description:
• Fluent written and spoken English. Our clients are US doctors. You will write to them and speak with them every day.
  • You own outcomes. You have handled client relationships and can tell us what you kept, what you lost and why. Haven't owned a client book yet? tell us honestly.
  • You bring bad news early, with a plan. You do not wait to be asked.
  • You write clearly and fast. If your writing needs a second pass to be understood, this is the wrong seat.
  • You can hold a doctor's respect. Calm, direct, prepared, unbothered by pushback.
  • You live in AI tools. You useClaude or similar every day, can show us how, and pick up new tools fast. This matters more to us than your resume.

You do not need to be a GoHighLevel expert on day one, but you must learn fast and be willing to build. You need to work 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Eastern, with your camera on.

Skunks on the table

Every line is true. If one makes you want to close the tab, that is useful for both of us. If they make you lean in, you are probably who we are looking for.

  • This is a fully remote position. If you do not have a quiet, productive place to work from home with reliable power and internet, this is not the right role for you.
  • Going quiet is the one thing that does not work here. Missed a deadline? Tell us. Stuck? Say "I hit a wall." Problems get named the same day, in the open.
  • No recipe, and the structure keeps moving. We are "building the plane while flying it," and pods, seats and clients change as we grow. The first 2 to 3 weeks are quiet. The people who thrive start digging before anyone asks.
  • The CEO is direct. Plain feedback, expected back. He loves being challenged and hates silence.
  • Doctors push back, and quality beats volume. Our clients are smart, busy and spending their own money, so you hold your ground with evidence. A cheap lead who cannot afford a $4,000 treatment is not a win. Compliance is non-negotiable: no guarantees, no definitive claims.
  • You are the last set of eyes. Errors that should have been caught in QA come out of the pod's bonus pool, just as retention and expansion grow it.

Our values: give a shit · better before bigger · sincere candor · move fast and fix it · prove it works · unimpeachable character.
attributes.projects:
WANTED! The BEST Remote Junior Client Success Manager In The World

To apply, answer the questions in the application form. One of them asks you to type exactly: "I actually read the instructions."

Most account managers forward emails and read reports out loud on calls. We are not looking for that person. Our clients are doctors who own cash-pay medical clinics. We are looking for the person they call first: the one who spots the problem before they do, tells them before they ask, and shows up with the fix already moving.

Who we are: a US-based growth consultancy for cash-pay medical practices. Our website says it plainly: marketing agencies suck, so we built Guidepost to be the exception. We run Meta and Google ads into funnels built in GoHighLevel, and every piece of work ties back to one question: did the clinic make money? You would join a pod (a CSM, a small, lean team with shared support) that owns clients end to end. Monthly client churn is under 1%.
attributes.functions:
• You own the relationship. The doctor emails you, Slacks you and gets on calls with you.
  • You turn requests into work. Every client ask becomes a ClickUp task the team can act on without a follow-up question, with the why attached. "Build a new landing page" is not a brief. "The heatmap shows people stop scrolling before the CTA, so the CTA moves above the fold" is. When it is something you can build, you build it.
  • You narrate the numbers. In two minutes, in plain English: what is working, what is not, and what is next.
  • You catch problems first. The client never discovers an issue we have not already told them about.
  • You spot the next win. Not a pitch. Arithmetic out loud with the client's own numbers until the next step is obvious.

This is not a messenger seat: from day one you also build GoHighLevel automations, workflows and landing pages, using AI to move fast. And if all you do on a call is read a report, you are not doing the job.

What a good month looks like

  • Every client request became a ClickUp task with enough context that nobody had to come back to you to ask what it meant.
  • You ran the client calls yourself. The CEO was not on them.
  • You built or fixed automations, workflows or pages yourself instead of leaving them in someone else's queue.
  • Your pod's daily client updates went out accurate, because you read them before they shipped and corrected the one that was wrong.
  • No client surprised anyone with a problem, and no client cancelled without the risk being visible weeks earlier.
  • You brought at least one expansion case built on a client's real numbers, or explained why the timing was wrong.

How we work

  • Reply to clients within 1 business hour, even if it is "got it, looking into it," with a real answer or a timeline within 24. Reply to internal Slack within 10 minutes.
  • Decisions live on the ClickUp task or in the client channel. Never in DMs.
  • Monday all-hands, 9:00 to 10:30 AM Eastern.

attributes.long_description:
Want to create a greener future for our cities?

Our vision is a future of affordable mobility services which support the environment. A transformation is taking place across our cities and, with Forest, we can all start building a healthier & more sustainable future for our urban communities.

Forest is a fast-growing and innovative micro-mobility company with a global team making transport more sustainable and affordable for London travellers. We combine easy to use micro-mobility solutions with a unique marketing platform to make rides cheaper and greener for our users and partners.

Our Values

Put People First

Our people are what makes forest forest. So we listen with care, lead with kindness and create a safe space where everyone can show up as their authentic self, being treated equally, respectfully and with no judgement. We do the right thing - for our employees and our users - even when no one is watching.

Build Together
We can’t do this alone. We believe in collaboration, transparency and keeping each other in the loop, even when the news is tough. We ask for help when we need it and enjoy supporting others. We're not afraid to hire people better than ourselves and celebrate strengths different to our own.

Inspire Trust
We trust people with autonomy and empower them to work in a way that enables their best performance. We give and encourage candid feedback and treat mistakes not as reasons for blame, but as opportunities to learn, grow, and strengthen how we work together.

Take Ownership
We start small, dream big, own our mistakes and learn from them to make progress happen. We don’t outsource accountability. We find solutions to problems before we’re asked to, and proactively take responsibility and ownership of our work.

Embrace Joy
We don't take ourselves too seriously and know the importance of having fun. Whether on a bike, on slack or in the office, we prioritise shared experiences, celebrating wins and having a laugh. We make work a place people want to be.

Unlock Innovation
We do things differently. We adapt to changes quickly, challenge assumptions, push boundaries, and aren’t afraid to experiment or fail. We prioritise curiosity over red tape, implementing creative solutions from small, incremental changes to major breakthroughs that continuously improve what we do.

Be the Best
"Good enough" isn't good enough when we’re building something that matters. We hire people who are the best in their field, we work hard and challenge each other to excel at what we do. We solve root causes rather than patch symptoms, choosing the right path over the easy one and balance speed with thoughtfulness.

Make an (actual) Impact
We’re doing something that’s bigger than us. We're building Forest with intention, substance and sustainability in mind, not as a PR exercise but as a reflection of who we are. No matter what your role is, we can all make a difference for our people, our users, and change how London moves.

Deep Relational Data Architecture Expertise — Proven ownership of complex production relational data models at real scale.

Strong PostgreSQL experience (Cocoon currently uses Aurora PostgreSQL).

AI-Native Engineering Capability— Demonstrated ability to use modern AI-assisted development tools to materially improve engineering productivity and quality, while applying the technical judgment needed to critically evaluate AI-generated work.

Production Engineering Discipline — Strong understanding of application security, automated testing, observability, reliability, performance and maintainability. Builds systems designed to operate reliably in production, not simply function in development.

Technical Leadership & Independent Judgment — Experience directing senior engineers and serving as a trusted technical authority. Comfortable making consequential decisions with incomplete information, surfacing risks early, challenging assumptions, and recommending a clear path forward.

Production Applied-AI Experience (Highly Preferred) — Meaningful hands-on experience implementing and operating production AI, LLM, agentic, multimodal, or computer-vision capabilities, including architecture, evaluation, retrieval, reliability, and production operations

Strong Cloud & Production Infrastructure Fluency — Experience with AWS-hosted production systems (EC2, S3, RDS/Aurora, IAM, VPC networking), containers, CI/CD and modern cloud deployment architecture.

How You Work

Owner's Mindset, Professional Maturity & Communication

  • Operates like an owner, not a ticket-taker.
  • Takes responsibility for outcomes, moves quickly without sacrificing quality, disagrees productively, communicates clearly, and credibly represents Cocoon with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

Genuine Engineering Craft

  • Still loves building software and is comfortable operating without a large engineering organization around them.

Thrives in a Startup Environment

  • Acts independently while collaborating effectively within a small team. Knows how to get things done and works quickly without requiring a high degree of oversight.
attributes.projects:
Cocoon connects property intelligence, homeowner engagement and service fulfillment to help homeowners better maintain and protect their homes while enabling insurance carriers and other partners to move from identifying property risk to addressing and verifying risk mitigation.

To take the next step in growing our business, we are seeking an exceptional Principal Engineer who will inherit our fully functional platform. We are looking for someone who wants to become a long-term member of Cocoon's core team, participate meaningfully in the company's success.

You will understand that system deeply, determine what should be preserved, identify what should be improved and lead the evolution of the platform's technical foundation in line with product and business strategy.

Serving as Cocoon's primary internal technical authority and source of technical truth, you will own technical architecture and engineering decisions in alignment with the company's product and business priorities.
attributes.functions:
Technical Architecture & Leadership

  • Serve as Cocoon's primary internal authority on backend architecture, data architecture, system design and engineering quality.
  • Own technical architecture and engineering decisions.
  • Spearhead Cocoon's efforts to integrate AI-driven capabilities into its products, platform and engineering workflows.

Hands-On Backend Engineering

  • Remain deeply hands-on in Cocoon's codebase and personally develop production software.
  • Enter an established codebase, understand it quickly and determine what should be retained, refactored or replaced.
  • Help shape product ideas and requirements alongside Cocoon team members before specifications are finalized.

Data Architecture

  • Lead evolution of Cocoon's existing data architecture into a sophisticated relational domain model.
  • Define schemas, relationships, data-access patterns and integrity standards.
  • Develop safe migration strategies for evolving an active production database.
  • Account for both structured and unstructured information as Cocoon's AI capabilities expand.
  • Build a data foundation capable of supporting substantially greater intelligence, automation and scale over time.

attributes.description:
Senior, and genuinely full stack. You’ve shipped and operated production systems end to end. You don’t need to be an expert in every layer on day one, but you should be someone who has repeatedly gone and learned the layer the problem was in.

Comfortable with loose requirements. You’ll often get a problem and a constraint, not a spec. You convert that into a plan, ask the two questions that actually matter, and start building.

A finisher. You can drive a project from a vague idea to shipped and stable — including the unglamorous last 20%.

AI-pilled, concretely. You’re already building with agents, not just autocompleting with them. You have opinions about what to hand to a model, how to verify its output, and where the leverage actually is. We’ll ask what you’ve automated.

Strong judgment about risk. We handle sensitive financial data for people who can’t afford for us to get it wrong. You know which corners are safe to cut and which aren’t.
attributes.projects:

You’ll also build the systems that make a four-person team move like a bigger one. 100% of our code is now written with AI, and we’re pushing further: agents that triage errors, open fix PRs, run our QA suite, audit our dependencies, and handle the recurring engineering work that would otherwise consume a headcount. Extending that toolchain isn’t a side project here, it’s a core part of the job.

attributes.title: AI Automation Engineer — Contract
attributes.description:
Real experience building agent systems that run unattended

This is the requirement we cannot flex on. We are not looking for someone who has used AI tools, or built a chat interface over a document set. We are looking for someone who has built harnesses — a model with tools, memory and a task loop, running on a schedule, doing work without a person in the conversation. Tell us about one you built and shipped. What it did, what it got wrong, how you found out, and what you changed. We are as interested in the failure handling as in the capability.

The discipline that makes a model safe to leave running

Some of what you build here touches federally regulated processes. Getting an answer mostly right is not good enough, and neither is escalating everything and calling it safe.

What separates an automation we can trust from a demo is the scaffolding around the model, and we have strong views on it:

  • Deterministic checks bracket every model step. Validate the inputs before the model sees them, and validate the output against rules that do not involve a model. The reasoning sits in the middle, and it never certifies its own work — a verdict on correctness comes from a check the model cannot influence.
  • Missing is a failure, not a pass. An empty result, a partial record, a field that did not populate — these fail loudly. The most expensive bugs in this class of system are the ones where nothing appeared to go wrong.
  • Every output traces to the exact inputs that produced it. When a number is questioned six weeks later, you can show which records, which version of the logic, and which run produced it.
  • Confidence thresholds are explicit. What the system handles alone, what it flags for a person, and what it refuses to decide — decided deliberately and written down, not emergent.

You do not need to have used those words. You do need to have learned the lesson some other way, and to recognize why it matters more here than in most places. If your instinct on finding compliance logic in an unversioned script is that it needs fixing before it needs extending, you will do well here.

Our stack — ideally you know some of this

  • Python or Node for the pipelines. We are not precious about which
  • Agent harnesses — the orchestration layer around the model, not just the model. Claude Code and similar coding agents, especially used across a team; custom harnesses you have built yourself; anything where you have had to decide what the loop does, where it stops, and what happens when a step fails. This is the part of the stack we care most about
  • Agent frameworks and tool protocols — MCP, function calling, whatever you have used to give a model real capability
  • Browser automation — some of what we need to reach has no API
  • SQL and analytical databases — our data platform is ClickHouse
  • ERP data — SAP Business One, though you do not need to have worked in it
  • Source control and CI as habits, not as process imposed on you
attributes.projects:
About the role

BluPax is a pharmaceutical distributor. A lot of what keeps the business running is still done by hand — people pulling data out of one system every morning, checking it against another, and re-entering the result somewhere else. We are building a development team to change that, and this is the role that does it. You would build the automation layer: agents that run on a schedule, connect to the systems we already use, do the work, and escalate only the exceptions that need a person. Not a chatbot. Not a pilot. Software that runs unattended and that people come to rely on.

The first project

Our compliance team handles controlled substances, and two of their daily processes are the first targets. One is a high-volume inventory report assembled by hand every morning before the day starts. The other is an order review that checks proposed orders against customer and sales history under federal thresholds
attributes.functions:
• Build scheduled, autonomous pipelines: fetch the data, do the work, produce the output, deliver it — without a human starting it
  • Design the exception path. Clean cases should complete silently; the ones that need attention should reach the right person with the context to act
  • Connect to the systems we run — our ERP, our data platform, third-party tools, and web interfaces where no API exists
  • Build the deterministic guardrails and audit trail underneath all of it — input validation, output checks the model cannot influence, and traceability from any result back to the records and logic version that produced it
  • Capture user corrections as a feedback signal, so the system’s accuracy is measurable and improves
  • Work directly with the people whose jobs you are changing, and understand a process properly before automating it
  • Leave behind something maintainable — documented, in source control, and operable by someone who is not you
